prompt: How did the paper train the network, should we augment training images, and what would our robustness test then measure?
suggestion: Distinguish training augmentation from testing on held-out images. Compare basic and corruption-augmented training under a fixed evaluation protocol.
decision: Refined by the user: start with plain training without horizontal flips.
reason: Establish the unaugmented baseline before considering augmentation.

prompt: Start training with a sensible training, validation and test split; train a baseline similar to the paper, perhaps without horizontal flipping.
actions: Implemented a paper-inspired 84,001-parameter CNN with no augmentation; audited decoded pixels; excluded 378 official-test overlaps and 920 repeated training copies; reserved 5,000 images per label for validation; preserved the official test set; selected checkpoints using validation loss only.
decision: No augmentation implemented at the user's request. Duplicate handling, exact split, optimizer and stopping settings selected by the assistant and documented in README.md and run configuration.
reason: Establish a reproducible baseline with no exact duplicate leakage and no test-driven model selection.
limitations: The paper's arXiv methods do not specify a training augmentation policy. This implementation is paper-inspired, not an exact reproduction. Near-duplicates were not checked.

prompt: We need checkpoints so training is saved, and the team uses this GitHub repository.
actions: Saved all 24 epoch checkpoints plus best.pt and last.pt; added atomic flushed checkpoint saves and resume support; verified resumed CPU training against uninterrupted training on synthetic data; added portable data-path checks and compact model/results export for Git, with a separate full-run archive.
decision: Checkpointing and team sharing implemented at the user's request; no remote GitHub publication performed.
result: Best validation-loss checkpoint: epoch 19. Validation accuracy 94.54%; official test accuracy 94.29%. Early stopping at epoch 24. Test results were not used to change the model.

prompt: Have this in a .ipynb Jupyter notebook file; that is where we are working.
actions: Created baseline_training.ipynb as the team's main workflow, with configuration, split audit, training/resume controls, checkpoint inspection, plots, validation examples, saved test results, and artifact export. Added direct Python-call support to the existing scripts and project-local Jupyter kernel setup.
decision: Notebook format implemented at the user's request. Default review mode reuses the completed run; new training and final test evaluation are explicit settings. Shared Python modules preserve one training implementation.

prompt: Do the visualizations please in the same notebook.
actions: Added section 4 to baseline_training.ipynb: split-count charts, exact-duplicate examples, fixed real/fake galleries, full-training brightness/contrast/saturation/Laplacian-variance distributions, sharpness extremes, a linked Plotly image explorer, and normalized Fourier spectra. Saved seven PNG figures and a numerical summary under results/eda_baseline_seed1; pinned widget dependencies and updated the README.
decision: Implemented notebook EDA at the user's request. Static outputs support team review; the clickable explorer requires a live kernel and local training data.
validation: Executed every notebook code cell; checked constant-color/checkerboard feature calculations, spectrum normalization, explorer click/path mapping and axis callbacks; verified baseline model, best/last checkpoints, test metrics and split-manifest checksums were unchanged.
limitations: EDA was added after baseline training. Only training pixels are explored; split-count/overlap charts use metadata for all splits. Class associations do not prove model reliance. Near-duplicates and semantic-category balance were not audited.

prompt: Push this to GitHub; before that, how can the team access the model without retraining?
actions: Prepared the notebook, compact selected model, Python implementation, saved results and EDA figures for the requested GitHub push. Added explicit teammate instructions for loading the included checkpoint in review mode or directly in Python; verified CPU inference from the compact checkpoint.
decision: The user authorized publishing these project changes to the existing team repository. Full runs, datasets, caches and the environment remain excluded by the existing sharing policy.

actions: Separated the baseline documentation into BASELINE.md and linked it from the notebook. Preparing a dedicated baseline-training-and-eda branch while preserving the remote main branch, its README, and Plotting_01.ipynb.
